memory_update.text: POWL should be tracked as a direct switchgear/electrical power systems candidate with strong backlog signals, but its market cap has moved slightly above the preferred underfollowed $300M-$10B range.

AZZ is a high-quality second-order underfollowed candidate because galvanizing for T&D structures, monopoles and lattice towers may benefit from grid buildout while being hidden under coatings/industrial-services labels.

WCC is a distributor/logistics candidate for transformer, switchgear, T&D hardware and data-center electrical products; later layers should validate whether backlog and supplier allocation create pricing power or only pass-through revenue.

HUBB is the reference benchmark for direct grid-component exposure, with Utility Solutions at 63% of 2025 revenue and products spanning transmission, distribution, substation, grid controls and utility meters.

Layer 2 should search specifically for US-listed conductor manufacturers, transformer-core/component suppliers, relay/protection specialists, utility-qualified niche vendors and regional grid-construction subcontractors below $10B market cap.

node: Grid transformers, high-voltage equipment, switchgear, and conductors
summary: Expanded the node around U.S.-listed grid equipment and second-order infrastructure suppliers. The strongest underfollowed lane candidates are Powell Industries for medium-voltage switchgear and electrical power systems backlog, AZZ for corrosion-protection/galvanizing exposure to transmission and distribution steel structures, and Wesco for utility/data-center electrical distribution and supply-chain visibility. Hubbell is included as a larger reference anchor because its Utility Solutions segment has unusually direct exposure to transmission, distribution, substation, grid controls, meters, arresters, insulators, connectors, bushings, cutouts and switches. No buy/sell view is implied.
